notes: PTCpedia's own Denrol article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-denrol.html, captured 20 Aug 2010) bills this character under the civilian name this record already carries as an aka, and, as the wiki's own secondary account, tells a career the held WWA record reaches only through its own title history: a June 1998 signing with Northeast Championship Wrestling, "which would eventually become the World Wrestling Alliance"; a WWA World Championship won 1 July 1999 and lost three days later, the shortest such reign the fed staged; an October 2002 near-career-ending attack by Jackson Kraven and the Cell in a Frozen Hell match at Rage in the Cage 2003 that answered it; The Franchise Players with Tracer Bullet, winning the Tag Team titles at Rage In The Cage IX and dropping them at Bourbon Street Brawl 2006; and a second United States Championship won on the Meltdown of 20 April 2009, ten years after the first. That last match is the one fact in this packet carried by two articles at once: PTCpedia's own Richie Stone article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-richie-stone.html, captured 20 Aug 2010) narrates the same no-disqualification Meltdown from the champion's side in the same words, down to Seth Copeland's interference deciding it — the two articles are a shared match narration, not two articles about one person, and Richie Stone has no held row. The article also has this character take a job as a WWA road agent while wrestling part time, which resolves the "WWA Road Agent" figure of that name in PTCpedia's own Albert Drabble and Elvis Hunt articles, where he signs both men at an independent show in Las Vegas in November 2008. Two further claims are recorded and not acted on. The article says this character's gimmick changes ran "from Father Denrol to The Denrol, and even D.E.N.R.O.L.", which would make father-denrol-wwa a persona of this one; the distinct guard on this record stands, because the WWA's own Royal Rumble text stages the two as separate physical entrants at once and a fed's own staging outranks a community wiki's career summary — both readings are recorded (#sources-disagree, #secondary-source-pivot) and the pair is worth a review-queue look. And it claims this character once ran a federation of his own under the WWA's umbrella era, losing it when the company reformed as one fed under its staged president; the federation label is left to the census's own unheld-federation pass and no promotion row is touched here.

notes: Billed only in PTC-forum card previews; not documented elsewhere in the WWA corpus. PTCpedia's own Andy McMirra article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-andy-mcmirra.html, captured 19 Aug 2010) tells this character's WWA career as a 2005 rookie debut, a boxing hiatus, a mid-2007 re-debut, the WWA United States Championship won at Birthday Bash 2007 and held "almost 7 months" before he was fired and stripped, a six-man Ultimate Glory match at Rage In The Cage XI in April 2008 alongside Seth Copeland, Dave Harley, Mal Somers, Denrol and Damian Thorne, and a January 2009 return; it bills him from Los Angeles, California, finishing with The Wipeout, and also claims a WWA Television Championship. Those are the wiki's own claims, not settled fact, and none is corroborated by the held WWA corpus, which reaches this character only through PTC-forum card previews of February–March 2006. The two accounts disagree about when he was in the WWA at all — the article's own timeline has him away from the company across 2006 — and both are recorded. PTCpedia's own Danny Vista article independently narrates the 2006 run this record holds from the other side: Vista's television debut against Andy McMirra on 20 February 2006, the feud it started, and its "Finish Him Off" cage blowoff at Rage In The Cage, which Vista won. The Television Championship that note reports as an uncorroborated claim is dated and populated by two PTCpedia articles read together: this character's own says he beat Elvis Hunt for it two weeks after a 23 February return, and lost it to Brandon Eagle in a triple-threat elimination at Revolution 2009 that also included Hunt; PTCpedia's own Elvis Hunt article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-elvis-hunt.html, captured 20 Aug 2010) narrates the same two matches from the other side, placing the title change on the Meltdown of 10 March and Hunt's own reign as beginning at Birthday Bash X. Both are the wiki's own claims; Elvis Hunt has no held row, and nothing in the held WWA corpus answers to either match.
